spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The conditional and unconditional arguments diverge at a precise interface: RH supplies a deterministic prime-sum majorant, while without RH one must suppress large-prime contributions statistically and encode exponentials as finite Dirichlet polynomials.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source records pointwise zeta moment estimates, including all beta under RH and beta at most four unconditionally. Under RH a deterministic inequality bounds log absolute zeta by a weighted prime sum. Unconditionally the proof instead uses averaged estimates. A truncated exponential identity expands exp(lambda P) into a finite Dirichlet polynomial indexed by Omega(n), with multiplicative coefficients g(p^k)=1/k! and exponentially small remainder on a bounded-P event.
directed.conceptual_reading: The key distinction is not merely a stronger constant under RH; it changes deterministic domination into exceptional-set management. Exponential truncation restores finite algebraic structure needed by mean-value theorems.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The truncated exponential is the bridge from an additive prime field to a multiplicative Dirichlet polynomial, allowing analytic moment machinery to act on the mollifier.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The truncation is uniform only where |lambda P| is controlled, and unconditional zeta moments stop at beta four in the cited input.
directed.uncertainty: Low for the methodological split and truncation role; medium for exact weights in the formula-sensitive displays.

supported: The span records averaged zeta moment upper bounds for all beta under RH and through beta 4 unconditionally, gives an RH-conditional deterministic prime-sum upper bound for log absolute zeta, and contrasts it with unconditional average control.
It expands a controlled exponential prime polynomial into a finite Dirichlet polynomial indexed by Omega(n), with g(p^k)=1/k! and an exponentially small remainder on the bounded-P event.
inference: The change from deterministic domination to exceptional-set management is a meaningful methodological distinction.
Finite exponential truncation supplies algebraic structure compatible with Dirichlet-polynomial mean values.
unsupported_or_imported: The phrase pointwise zeta moment estimates is inaccurate: Propositions 2.1 and 2.2 are expectations over the random shift tau, hence averaged moment estimates; only the separate logarithmic inequality is pointwise in t.

missed_mechanism: The candidate should preserve the sharp distinction between an averaged moment input and a deterministic pointwise majorant.
revision_instructions: Replace pointwise zeta moment estimates with averaged one-location moment estimates over tau, while reserving pointwise or deterministic language for inequality (2.3); retain the remaining truncation analysis.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: For a shrinking interval, early prime blocks are shared across nearly all points and therefore cannot generate spatial abundance. The proof begins at a θ-dependent scale aligned with the interval's correlation length, bounds the discarded common part, and counts locations that cross a slightly raised barrier in every retained block so Paley-Zygmund can control their volume.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source sets J(θ)=1 for θ≥0 and approximately K|θ|+1 for -1<θ<0. In the negative-θ case, Corollary 2.12 bounds the contribution of blocks before J(θ). It defines N as the Lebesgue measure of h for which every retained P_j(h) exceeds a threshold x_j, chosen slightly above an even division of γ log log T. Summing thresholds and combining with the early-block bound reduces the desired high-point-volume event to showing N≥(log T)^{Eθ(γ)-η}, to be proved by Paley-Zygmund.
directed.conceptual_reading: The construction distinguishes common signal from multiplicity-producing fluctuations. Removing scales longer than the observation window prevents shared randomness from being miscounted as many independent high points.
directed.representation_or_bridge: J(θ) maps geometric interval width to the first usable prime scale; N converts simultaneous blockwise barrier crossings into a measurable set of total high points suitable for first- and second-moment analysis.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The blockwise barrier event is a sufficient, stronger event, not an equivalence with exceeding the total height. This span only performs the reduction; concentration of N still requires one- and two-point estimates.
directed.uncertainty: The scale alignment is explicit, but several braces, threshold factors, and powers are extraction-fragmented, so exact definitions need scan verification.

supported: The source chooses the first retained block J(theta), obtains high-probability uniform smallness of the earlier-block sum for negative theta, and defines N by simultaneous barrier crossings in every retained block.
It states that the early-block bound together with a lower bound on N is sufficient for the desired high-point-volume event and reduces the task to Paley-Zygmund.
The candidate correctly warns that the blockwise event is sufficient rather than equivalent and that the one- and two-point work is still outstanding.
inference: Mapping interval width to a first usable prime scale is suggested by J(theta), but the exact source span establishes the reduction through the early-block maximum bound rather than through an independent correlation calculation.
unsupported_or_imported: The claims that the discarded early blocks are 'shared across nearly all points' and 'cannot generate spatial abundance' are not established in this span; they import the later correlation interpretation.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: 'Common signal versus multiplicity-producing fluctuations' is useful intuition but is too categorical unless marked as an inference rather than source-grounded mathematics.
context_or_ocr_risk: The threshold x_j and several set braces and powers are fragmented; exact definitions require scan verification.
missed_mechanism: The source-grounded reason available here is the uniform high-probability smallness of the pre-J(theta) sum, not a proved statement that those blocks are common to all points.
revision_instructions: Rewrite the spontaneous and conceptual readings around the explicit reduction: the early-block contribution is uniformly small on a high-probability event, so retained blockwise crossings suffice.
If the shared-correlation interpretation is kept, label it explicitly as a later-motivated inference rather than a conclusion of this span.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: When a sharp Gaussian asymptotic is unnecessary, a factorial 2l-moment bound turns coefficient energy into rapid exceptional-set control. Its flexibility comes from sacrificing sharp constants while retaining the decisive dependence l!(Σ|a(p)|²/p)^l.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Lemma A.4 bounds the averaged 2lth power of the prime Dirichlet polynomial Σ_{p≤x} a(p)p^{-1/2-iτ} by a constant times l! times (Σ_{p≤x}|a(p)|²/p)^l, for 2≤x≤T and natural l satisfying the stated restriction that x^l remain below the averaging scale T/log T.
directed.conceptual_reading: This is a robust energy-to-tail converter: coefficient L2 mass controls high moments, and Markov can trade the factorial growth against a chosen exceptional threshold without resolving the full distribution.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is from a random-height Dirichlet polynomial to its weighted coefficient energy; factorial moments then feed union bounds, discretized maxima, and negligible-error estimates.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The estimate is crude and does not supply Gaussian asymptotics or covariance information. It must not be used outside the length-moment admissibility condition.
directed.uncertainty: The compact inequality is conceptually clear, but extraction obscures the exact comparison symbol in the admissibility condition and some normalization; scan verification is required.

supported: The span states a crude 2l-th moment upper bound for a prime Dirichlet polynomial in terms of l! times the l-th power of its weighted coefficient energy.
The candidate correctly distinguishes this estimate from Gaussian asymptotics and explains its use with Markov-type exceptional-set bounds.
inference: Describing the lemma as an energy-to-tail converter is a faithful operational reading of the moment inequality.
unsupported_or_imported: The normalized text has lost the comparison symbol in the admissibility condition between x^l and T/log T, so the candidate's assertion that x^l is below the averaging scale reconstructs a direction not safely present in the frozen span.
context_or_ocr_risk: Both the admissibility comparison and some norm typography are extraction-damaged; the exact condition and normalization require scan verification.
revision_instructions: Until the scan is checked, state only that the bound holds under the lemma's extraction-damaged admissibility relation between x^l and T/log T; do not supply the missing comparison direction as source-grounded text.
